ideas.name: Threshold Rebalancing Price Pressure
ideas.claim: When stocks are overweight relative to allocation targets, institutional rebalancing is associated with lower next-day equity returns. The paper distinguishes an intra-month threshold signal from its month-end calendar signal.
ideas.quote: When stocks are overweight, funds sell stocks and buy bonds, leading to a decrease in equity returns of 17 basis points over the next day.
ideas.mechanism: Institutional portfolio rebalancing creates equity selling pressure when equity weights exceed targets.

rules.market: S&P 500 futures and 10-year Treasury note futures
rules.filters: Stocks overweight relative to target allocation

not_stated: threshold associated specifically with the quoted 17-basis-point effect
ideas.claimed_result: The paper reports a 17-basis-point decrease in next-day equity returns when stocks are overweight; its threshold signal also negatively predicts subsequent S&P 500 returns relative to 10-year Treasury note returns.
required_data: Portfolio allocation and rebalancing threshold assumptions

ideas.name: Futures Roll Spread Volatility
ideas.claim: S&P 500 E-mini calendar-spread volatility rose as contract expiration approached in the study's 2016 sample.
ideas.quote: In the U.S., India, and China, spread volatility is confirmed to rise as expiration approaches.
ideas.mechanism: Futures positions roll from the front contract to the next contract as expiration approaches.

rules.timeframe: Daily; 15 trading days up to and including expiration

not_stated: numerical magnitude of the volatility increase
ideas.claimed_result: The paper reports a statistically significant relationship between roll-period day and calendar-spread Parkinson volatility for the U.S. sample.
required_data: Front- and next-contract S&P 500 E-mini futures prices
